feature: Commander availability — the dot says owned, the marker says what that is worth
note:
The two panels on `/commanders/[slug]` that draw a card's claim: Role Coverage (chips at desktop, rows at phone) and the synergy panel (a slot before the toggle at desktop, the meta line at phone). Both were rebuilt on `loadAvailability`, where they previously read `committedTo` — the first deck naming a card, which knows nothing about how many copies are free.

WHAT THE PICTURE IS FOR, and what it is not. `pnpm probe:commander-availability` MEASURES these surfaces — the chip's 28px against a name that must not wrap, the marker's resolved type, the key pip's baseline, the slot's fixed width — and a contact sheet cannot see any of that. These cells exist for the thing measurement cannot do: showing that both panels got the feature at both widths, which is exactly the class of failure that shipped here once already (the price reached the phone panel and not the desktop one, and every component test passed).

PRECONDITION, and this round CREATED it: the account must have `user_prefs.about_version_seen` at or above `ABOUT_VERSION`, which this feature bumped to 3. Since #658 `proxy.ts` redirects a reader below it to `/about?next=…`, and `contact-sheet.mjs` cannot clear that itself. Every `wait` below names something only the finished panel draws, never `h1` — both this route and the About page render one inside `<main>`, so a looser wait would resolve against the interstitial and the cell would count as REACHED while photographing About. A gated run fails its cells, which is the good failure.

The probe does clear the gate, by pressing `Got it` the way a reader would; the sheet runner has no such step, so acknowledge the version on the account once before expecting cells from this file.

`COMMANDER_AVAILABILITY_SLUG` is yours to supply and should name a commander the account owns cards for — Role Coverage is built from the owned pool, so a commander with no owned staples draws the panel's empty state and the cells photograph a feature that is correctly absent.

NO COMMA-SEPARATED WAITS, and this file learned it the hard way. `onPage` prefixes `main ` onto the selector, and a prefix applies to the FIRST alternative only — `main li a, li b` scopes `a` and leaves `b` matching the whole document. The phone cell passed that way against an unscoped selector while the desktop cell timed out on the scoped one, which reads as a width-specific defect and is nothing of the kind. One selector per row.

The synergy slot is TWO rows, not one width-agnostic row. The 88px slot is desktop only — the phone puts the same clause on the existing meta line, with no column of its own — so one selector cannot serve both, and a shared row fails the width that is working correctly.

THE ABOUT ENTRY IS NOT A CELL HERE, and that is a limitation rather than a scope decision. `/about` renders no per-entry anchor — chapters get `id="chapter-NN"` and entries get nothing — and `contact-sheet.mjs` has no scroll verb, so an entry in chapter 02 sits below the fold with nothing to wait on. Waiting on `#chapter-02` instead would resolve instantly and photograph the top of the page: a cell that reads as coverage while showing none of the entry it claims to cover, which is worse than an absent row.

What covers it instead is `about.test.ts`, which asserts the entry exists, that a figure is registered under its id, and that no entry ships undrawn — the last of those is the gate that caught this feature arriving without one. A per-entry anchor would make this a cell; that is a change to the About page, not to this inventory.

WHAT THE CELLS ACTUALLY SHOW, stated so the next reader does not overrate them. Both panels sit below the fold on a phone and well down the page on desktop, and the runner has no scroll verb — so a cell photographs the top of the commander page with the panel it names small or off-screen. Each cell therefore evidences that the ROUTE was reached and rendered at that width, which is the failure class this feature actually shipped once (the price reached the phone panel and not the desktop one). It does not evidence the marks themselves.

`pnpm probe:commander-availability` is the stronger artifact and the one to run: it measures the chip's 28px against a name that must not wrap, the marker's resolved size and family at each width, the key pip's baseline and the slot's fixed width — none of which a picture at this scale could show.

THE PHONE WAIT NAMES THE ROW, not a shape other controls share. `button[class*="rounded-[8px]"]` alone also matches the synergy panel's disclosure, and `View details for` alone also matches every synergy row's card trigger — so either half by itself lets the cell pass with Role Coverage absent entirely, photographing a surface it does not name. Both together are `CoverageRow` and nothing else.

THE PHONE SYNERGY WAIT ANCHORS ON THE ROW'S TOGGLE, not on a marker. It named `tracking-[0.02em]`, which is the ROLE COVERAGE marker's class — the synergy row's marker does not carry it — so the cell could resolve on a CoverageRow while the synergy panel was still absent, and would also have failed on a perfectly valid panel whose every owned card has a spare copy and therefore draws no marker at all. `li button[aria-pressed]` is the row's own select toggle: present on every synergy row, and on nothing else.

shares.note: Both panels render the marker directly, with no wrapper, so each row's `view` is the file that imports it. The dot is deliberately NOT the shared binding: `OwnershipDot` is drawn by a dozen surfaces that have nothing to do with this feature, so naming it would pass on files this round never touched.
